WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = S * (c_step * Tc) + (Ts + tp) + S * (tsw + tsync)

where.H: Number of links along the path (hop_count from route)
where.Ts: Serialization time on the link for the given payload at 100 Mbps
where.tsw: Switching delay per switch (1 us, cut-through)
where.tsync: Time synchronization error budget per switch (1 us)
where.c_step: Per-switch cycle advance = floor((Ts + tp)/Tc) + 1 (accounts for oversized frames spanning multiple cycles)

notes: If Ts + tp <= Tc then c_step = 1 and each switch adds exactly one CQF cycle (50 us).
If Ts + tp > Tc then c_step >= 2, meaning a frame transmission/reception spans multiple cycles before it can be forwarded in the next CQF transmit window.
Final hop to the destination adds Ts + tp (there is no additional CQF cycle beyond the last switch).
Switching and time-synchronization margins are added once per switch as a conservative bound.

missing_inputs: Exact L2 framing overhead (MAC header, VLAN tag, preamble, SFD, IFG) not provided; Ts was computed from payload only.
Exact CQF receive/transmit window partition per cycle not provided; assumed full-cycle windows for PCP=7 TT traffic.
Whether frame preemption (802.3br/802.1Qbu) is enabled is not specified; assumed not used.
Exact per-hop gate alignment jitter budget besides the provided 1 us time sync error is not specified.
End-station (ES) CQF participation details not given; assumed the source starts at cycle boundary with offset 0 as stated.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_f = N_sw * C + N_links * t_prop + N_sw * t_sw + t_sync

variable_definitions.N_sw: number of switches on the path (i.e., count of SWxx nodes in the route)
variable_definitions.N_links: number of links (hop_count from the given route)
variable_definitions.t_sw: switching latency per switch (1 us, cut-through)
variable_definitions.t_sync: time synchronization error budget (1 us, applied once end-to-end)

assumptions: CQF two-queue operation with global odd/even cycle alignment; first egress at first switch occurs in the next cycle relative to the source emission at offset 0.
One cycle per traversed switch (pipeline).
Per-hop serialization and propagation are absorbed in the cycle term provided they fit the per-cycle budget (feasibility check reported per flow).
End-to-end delay is measured until the last bit is received at the destination.
WCD_calculation.per-cycle_feasibility_check: For each flow, t_ser = payload_bytes * 8 / 100 Mb/s = payload_bytes * 0.08 us. The per-hop CQF budget is C - (t_prop + t_sw + t_sync) = 47 us. A flow is feasible per hop if t_ser <= 47 us.

missing_inputs: Exact L2 frame sizing (preamble, SFD, IFG, MAC, VLAN/TSN tag overheads).
Whether end systems are CQF-gated or only switches are (affects initial waiting term).
Whether time synchronization error should be budgeted per hop or once end-to-end.
Fragmentation/segmentation policy for payloads that exceed the per-cycle serialization budget.
Exact gate open/close offsets per port (would refine per-hop cycle assignment and guard bands).

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_f = h*C + h*(L*8/R) + h*d_prop + (h-1)*d_sw + h*(2*epsilon)

where.h: hop_count (number of links in the route)
where.L: payload size in bytes (one frame per period)
where.R: link rate in bits/us (100 Mbps = 100 bits/us) so L*8/R = 0.08*L us
where.d_sw: switching delay per switch (1 us, cut-through)
where.epsilon: time synchronization error (1 us); 2*epsilon margin per hop (ingress+egress gate)

notes: CQF double-buffering induces <= 1 cycle per hop; with start offset set to 0 at the source, we count h cycles for h links.
All TT flows use PCP=7 with 2-queue CQF (odd cycles queue 7, even cycles queue 6).
Serialization is computed from payload only; no L2 overheads included (see missing_inputs).
Number of switches on an ES-to-ES path equals (h - 1).
Hypercycle (LCM of all flow periods and cycle 50 us) = 375000 us; used for network-wide periodic alignment context only.

missing_inputs: Exact Ethernet frame size on the wire (L2 header, VLAN tag, preamble/SFD, IFG). Payload-only serialization assumed.
CQF gate control lists (GCLs), offsets per flow, and explicit per-cycle slotting/guard bands.
Whether source end-stations implement CQF gating (we assumed start offset = 0 and no extra source-cycle wait).
Cut-through forwarding threshold (header length before egress) which could shave serialization overlap.
Any preemption (802.1Qbu/802.3br) not specified; assumed not used.
Clock sync budget apportionment across hops (we used 2*epsilon per hop as margin).

WCD_calculation.equation: For flow i with hop count h_i: WCD_i = h_i * C + h_i * T_prop + (h_i - 1) * T_sw + h_i * T_sync

variables.T_sw: Cut-through switching delay per switch (1 µs)
variables.T_sync: Time synchronization error budget per hop (1 µs)

notes: Offsets at sources are set to 0 as requested.
CQF imposes at most one-cycle queuing per hop; the cycle term h_i*C captures this.
Serialization time is not added on top of the cycle term, assuming it is budgeted inside the cycle; it is reported for feasibility checking only.
Feasibility check: T_tx = payload_bytes * 8 / (100 Mbps) = 0.08 * payload_bytes (µs). If T_tx > C, a CQF schedule with 2 buffers and C=50 µs is infeasible for that frame on any hop.

missing_inputs: Exact L2 frame overhead (preamble, SFD, MAC, VLAN, FCS) and IFG to compute serialization precisely
Per-port gate open/close times or offsets relative to cycle start
Guard band requirements per port (including preemption usage if any)
Clarification whether the 1 µs time synchronization error applies per hop or network-wide
Confirmation whether source end-systems also use CQF gating (which could add up to one extra cycle at the source in worst case)

where.h: hop_count (number of links in the provided path)
where.d_prop_last: propagation on the last hop (1 µs)
where.t_ser(P): serialization on last hop = (P bytes * 8) / 100 Mbps = 0.08*P µs

One CQF cycle of queuing per hop is included via h*T.
Only the last-hop serialization and propagation are added outside the cycle budget; prior hops are absorbed by CQF’s per-hop cycle.
WCD_calculation.hypercycle_computation: LCM of {all flow periods, 50 µs} = 375000 µs

equations: WCD_us = (h * n_tx_cycles * C) + (h * P + (h - 1) * S_sw + T_sync)
Using P = 1 µs/link, S_sw = 1 µs/switch, T_sync = 1 µs, C = 50 µs ⇒ WCD_us = (50 * h * n_tx_cycles) + 2h
notes: CQF peristaltic model is assumed: frames received in cycle n are transmitted in cycle n+1 (with two alternating queues).
When a frame’s serialization time exceeds one cycle, it occupies n_tx_cycles consecutive cycles on each egress.
Cut-through switches eliminate store-and-forward latency but do not remove the CQF cycle-to-cycle transfer.

missing_inputs: Exact Ethernet L2 overheads (MAC header, VLAN tags, preamble/SFD, IFG) per frame are not provided; serialization time was computed from payload only.
Whether end stations implement CQF gating exactly like switches (assumed yes).
Exact cycle boundary alignment strategy at all nodes (assumed perfect sync with 1 µs global margin).
Gate open/close sub-windows per PCP inside a cycle (assumed sufficient to carry required n_tx_cycles per hop).

all_parameters_used.hypercycle_derivation: LCM(50 µs, all flow periods) = 375000 µs

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = h * C + h * d_prop + (h - 1) * d_sw + ε_sync, where h = hop_count (number of links on the path), C = CQF cycle duration, d_prop = per-link propagation delay, d_sw = per-switch cut-through switching delay, ε_sync = time synchronization error
WCD_calculation.simplification_for_given_constants: With C=50, d_prop=1, d_sw=1, ε=1, WCD_us = 52 * h
WCD_calculation.how_h_is_counted: hop_count from the provided route equals the number of links (ES->SW and SW->SW and SW->ES). Number of switches on path = hop_count - 1.

missing_inputs: Frame serialization/overhead model: Only payload sizes are given. Without full L2 frame size (headers, preamble, IFG) the exact serialization time is unknown.

Feasibility with 50 µs CQF cycle at 100 Mbps: several payloads (e.g., ~1400 B) would take >50 µs to serialize on a single link, which violates the single-cycle transmission assumption for CQF unless preemption or larger cycle time is used. Preemption was not allowed and no larger cycle was specified; therefore serialization was excluded from WCD to avoid contradiction.
Application of time synchronization error per-hop vs. end-to-end was not specified. Here it is applied once end-to-end.
Exact TT gate schedules/offsets per port were not provided. Source offset was set to 0 per instruction; worst-case additional misalignment at ingress was not modeled beyond ε_sync.

WCD_calculation.equation: For a flow f with H = hop_count (links), S = number of switches on path, payload P (Bytes): s = 8*P / (100e6) seconds = 0.08*P microseconds; WCD_f = (S * T_cycle) + (H * d_prop) + (S * d_sw) + (H * s) + t_sync_err.
notes: CQF contributes exactly one cycle per switch traversal when source is aligned to cycle start (offset = 0).
Propagation and serialization are per link; switching delay is per switch.
This yields a deterministic bound without needing exact gate schedules since all TT traffic is assumed aligned to CQF windows.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_us = A0 + (H_sw * C) + (L_links * t_ser_per_link) + (L_links * t_prop) + (H_sw * t_sw) + ε

variables.A0: worst-case source alignment to CQF gate = C = 50 us
variables.H_sw: number of switches along the path (hop_count - 1)
variables.L_links: number of links along the path (hop_count)

WCD_calculation.simplified_equation: Since A0 + (H_sw * C) = 50 + 50*(L_links - 1) = 50*L_links, and (H_sw * t_sw) + ε + (L_links * t_prop) = (L_links - 1) + 1 + L_links = 2*L_links, we get WCD_us = L_links * (50 + 2 + 0.08*payload_B) = L_links * (52 + 0.08*payload_B).
WCD_calculation.note: All links are 100 Mbps, cut-through switches with 1 us switching delay; CQF adds one cycle per switching hop and worst-case one cycle alignment at the source.
